note.explanation: A magnetic field describes the region around a magnet where another magnetic object can feel a force. Magnetic lines of force show the field’s pattern and direction. Lines close together mean a stronger field; lines farther apart mean a weaker field.
examples: A compass needle placed near a magnet turns because it experiences a magnetic force.
In a horseshoe magnet, the field is almost uniform in the gap between its poles, except near the edges.
note.checkAnswer: Magnetic field strength is greater where the magnetic lines of force are closer together.
note.simple: A magnet affects magnetic objects around it, even when they are not touching it. The space where this effect happens is its magnetic field.
note.checkQuestion: Where is a magnetic field stronger: where its lines are close together or far apart?
note.title: Magnetic Fields Around Magnets
steps: Look at the pattern of magnetic lines of force around a magnet.
Use the N-pole of a compass needle to find the field direction at a point.
Compare the spacing of the lines: closer lines show a stronger field.
Remember that fields of nearby magnets combine; they can cancel at a neutral point.
note.answer: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where another magnetic object experiences a force.

options: The region where a magnetic object can experience a force
The space inside a magnet only
The path followed by an electric current
The region where gravity disappears
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes a magnetic field?
rationales: This is correct because a magnetic field is the region around a magnet where another magnetic object experiences a force.
This is incorrect because a magnetic field extends around the magnet, not only inside it.
This is incorrect because a current path does not define a magnetic field.
This is incorrect because a magnetic field does not make gravity disappear.

options: A line joining the two poles inside a magnet only
A line that shows the path of a magnetic compass needle
A line along which iron filings cannot move
A line that always points towards the south pole of Earth
mcqs.stem: What does a magnetic line of force represent in the field-pattern method?
rationales: This is incorrect because the lines describe the field pattern around the magnet, not only a path inside it.
This is correct because a compass needle moves along the magnetic lines of force.
This is incorrect because iron filings arrange themselves to show the field pattern.
This is incorrect because the direction depends on the magnetic field at the point, not always on Earth’s south pole.

options: By the direction of the compass needle’s N-pole
By the direction of the compass needle’s S-pole
By the colour of the magnet
By the size of the compass
mcqs.stem: How is the direction of the magnetic field at a point identified?
rationales: This is correct because the field direction is the direction indicated by the compass needle’s N-pole.
This is incorrect because the textbook defines the direction using the N-pole.
This is incorrect because magnet colour does not identify field direction.
This is incorrect because compass size does not identify field direction.

options: The lines are closer together
The lines are farther apart
There are no lines around the poles
The lines form a straight line
mcqs.stem: What spacing of magnetic lines indicates a stronger magnetic field?
rationales: This is correct because closer field lines indicate a stronger magnetic field.
This is incorrect because widely spaced lines indicate a weaker field.
This is incorrect because the field is particularly strong near the poles, where lines are close together.
This is incorrect because line spacing, not straightness, indicates relative field strength.

options: They spread out into separate straight rays
They go around a magnet in space, although a diagram may show only one plane
They exist only between the two poles
They stop at the edge of the paper
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly describes the magnetic field around a bar magnet?
rationales: This is incorrect because magnetic field lines are not described as separate straight rays.
This is correct because the field extends all around the magnet, while a drawing may show only one plane.
This is incorrect because the magnetic field is not limited to the space between the poles.
This is incorrect because the edge of a drawing does not stop the real magnetic field.

options: The fields of the two magnets cancel at that point
The magnet has no poles at that point
The compass has stopped working
The field is strongest at that point
mcqs.stem: What is meant by a neutral point between two magnets?
rationales: This is correct because a neutral point is where the field due to one magnet cancels the field due to the other.
This is incorrect because the neutral point does not mean the magnets lack poles.
This is incorrect because a neutral point is explained by cancellation of fields, not compass failure.
This is incorrect because cancellation means the resultant field is zero there, not strongest.

options: It is almost uniform between the poles, except near the edges
It is strongest only outside the gap
It has no field between the poles
It changes direction at every point in the gap
mcqs.stem: How is the magnetic field between the poles of a horseshoe magnet described?
rationales: This is correct because the field is almost uniform between the poles except near the edges.
This is incorrect because the textbook describes the field in the gap as almost uniform.
This is incorrect because field lines cross the gap between the poles.
This is incorrect because a uniform field does not change direction at every point in the gap.

options: The compass needle becomes a permanent magnet
Iron filings become tiny magnets by magnetic induction
The glass plate becomes magnetic
The filings melt and form lines
mcqs.stem: Why do iron filings arrange themselves around a bar magnet in a field pattern?
rationales: This is incorrect because the experiment explains the pattern by the filings becoming tiny magnets.
This is correct because magnetic induction makes the iron filings tiny magnets that form a pattern when the glass is tapped.
This is incorrect because the glass plate is used to hold the filings and is not said to become magnetic.
This is incorrect because the filings do not melt; they arrange into a pattern.

examTips: This section can be tested with short-answer definitions, especially magnetic field and magnetic lines of force.
For a definition, include both the key idea and its condition: a magnetic field is around a magnet, and another magnetic object experiences a force there.
For field strength, state the relationship clearly: closer lines mean a stronger field; farther-apart lines mean a weaker field.
If asked about a neutral point, explain that the fields due to two magnets cancel there.
When a question asks for a field direction, refer to the direction indicated by the N-pole of a compass needle.

explain.title: Magnetic field
explain.body: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where an other magnetic object experiences a force on it.

explain.title: Seeing the field pattern
explain.body: Iron filings placed on a glass plate over a bar magnet become tiny magnets through magnetic induction. When the plate is gently tapped, the filings form a pattern that shows the magnetic field.

explain.title: Magnetic lines of force
explain.body: The pattern can be shown by lines that correspond to the path of the filings. These lines are called magnetic lines of force. A small compass can also be used to draw them.

explain.title: Field direction
explain.body: The direction of the magnetic field at any point in space is the direction indicated by the N-pole of a magnetic compass needle placed at that point.

explain.title: Field strength
explain.body: The strength of the magnetic field is proportional to the number of magnetic lines of force passing through unit area placed perpendicular to the lines. Lines close together indicate a stronger field; lines farther apart indicate a weaker field.

mistakes: Do not define a magnetic field as the magnet itself; it is the region around the magnet where another magnetic object experiences a force.
Do not use the compass needle’s S-pole to state the field direction; use the direction indicated by its N-pole.
Do not say a field is weaker where lines are close together; closer lines mean a stronger field.
Do not treat a neutral point as a place where the magnets have no poles; it is where their magnetic fields cancel.
Do not assume the field exists only in the plane shown in a diagram; the field extends in space all around the magnet.
